routeInventory.evidence: Calls getAnalysisReadinessForCompany first and redirect()s on any non-ready reason. Verified for every reason value: NEVER_ANALYZED, RUN_IN_PROGRESS (both PENDING and RUNNING, manufactured directly in Postgres, not just via the orchestrator), RUN_NOT_READY via a manufactured FAILED-only run, RUN_NOT_READY via a manufactured PARTIAL run (AUDIT-F3's own status), STALE_DOCUMENTS_SINCE_LAST_RUN via a document inserted with a bare prisma.document.create (not through uploadDocumentAction), and a same-tick 'second tab' race where a document is inserted between two back-to-back ReviewPage() calls with no caching layer to smooth it over.

routeInventory.route: /{companyId}/onboarding/review/chunk/{chunkId} (the 'view in context' link from a candidate card, or direct URL)
routeInventory.evidence: Does not import or call getAnalysisReadinessForCompany. Dynamically confirmed: for a NEVER_ANALYZED company, this route renders successfully (no redirect, no notFound) where /onboarding/review itself would refuse to serve. However its data layer (getChunkContext) is a bare DocumentChunk lookup with zero awareness of ExtractionCandidate or ClaimReviewItem - it renders only raw source text the user's own upload already contains, never an analysis conclusion, a candidate value, a review status, or a ClaimReviewItem. It is a real, ungated route, but not a findings-consuming one, and not the same bypass shape AUDIT-F6 described (presenting analysis as settled). Recorded here so a future reader does not have to re-derive this.

viewFindingsLinkVerification.goldenPathReproducedIndependently: A manufactured COMPLETED_WITH_REVIEW run + a manufactured ClaimReviewItem (never produced via runContractAnalysis/the real pipeline, to test the rendering path independently of pipeline mechanics) is genuinely visible in ReviewPage's real rendered HTML output via renderToStaticMarkup, including its own rationale and sourceEvidence text - confirms getClaimReviewItemsForCompany's output is real, non-empty, ClaimReviewItem-aware content end to end, not merely 'does not crash'.

residualObservationFound.description: AnalysisRun.reviewItemCount is a denormalized snapshot taken once at run-completion time and is never recomputed when resolveClaimReview later resolves the items it counted. After resolving the single open ClaimReviewItem for a completed run (via the real resolveClaimReview function, action ACCEPT), the AnalysisRun row's reviewItemCount remains 1, the real documents-page 'Contract analysis' status card (its exact async ContractAnalysisStatusCard component, invoked directly from the real page's own returned element tree) still renders '1 open review item(s)' and a 'view findings' link, but the real /onboarding/review page it links to now renders zero items in its 'Contract analysis findings' card (correct with respect to the resolved item's new status, since getClaimReviewItemsForCompany defaults to OPEN_REVIEW only).
residualObservationFound.rationale: AUDIT-F6's own defect was the link's DESTINATION being structurally blind to ClaimReviewItem (a persisted OPEN_REVIEW row was provably invisible there). That is genuinely fixed - the destination now correctly reflects real ClaimReviewItem status, including correctly excluding resolved items. The residual gap found here is different and narrower: the BADGE that invites the click can overstate the current open-item count once items have been resolved after the run completed. This does not let anyone treat unanalyzed or stale content as analysis-complete (the direction of the original AUDIT-F6 risk) - if anything it errs toward over-caution (implying more outstanding review work than actually remains), and it never produces a crash, an empty destination masquerading as full, or a false 'nothing to review' state. Reported for completeness per this recertification's explicit mandate to verify the link end-to-end, but not treated as reopening FINDING-7's core bypass concern.

dispositionRationale: The core AUDIT-F6 concern - 'the actual product flow can still bypass authoritative contract analysis entirely' - could not be falsified despite deliberately adversarial, fresh routes and manufactured DB states that neither Workstream F's own test nor the prior recertification exercised: a company with zero documents and zero runs, a FAILED-only run, PENDING and RUNNING runs, a PARTIAL run (AUDIT-F3's own status), a document inserted through a path other than uploadDocumentAction, and a same-tick two-tab race all correctly block on the real, unmodified /onboarding/review route via the real getAnalysisReadinessForCompany predicate, with no caching or memoization gap found. The one genuinely ungated route discovered (review/chunk/[chunkId]) exposes no analysis-derived or findings content and is not the bypass shape this finding describes. The 'view findings' link's destination genuinely renders real, non-empty, ClaimReviewItem-aware content end to end (confirmed independently, not merely via Workstream F's own fixture) - the one residual gap found (a denormalized reviewItemCount badge that can go stale after resolution) is a distinct, narrower, non-safety-direction issue (over-caution, never a false 'analysis complete/nothing to review' signal) that does not recreate or resemble the original structural-blindness defect, and is disclosed for completeness rather than treated as grounds to reopen this finding.
